text.p: Property developer Hudson Conway Ltd said it was very satisfied with the performance of Melbourne's Crown Casino and would consider investments in other major projects due to its strong cash position.

The company, which earlier reported a flat 1995/96 net profit of A$25.7 million against A$25.3 million a year ago, is the largest shareholder in Crown Casino Ltd with a 37.5 percent stake. Crown's 1995/96 net profit rose to A$58.4 million from A$33.2 million.
Plans to open the casino's permanent site in the Southbank complex in early 1997 were on schedule, Hudson Conway said.
"The group continues to maintain an emphasis on liquidity, with cash reserves of A$192.4 million at 30 June," it said.
"These results ensure that the group is positioned to consider and, where appropriate, to invest in major projects."
The company said it had begun construction of a residential and resort project called Crown Towers on Queensland's Gold Coast with completion set for the end of 1997.
Early apartment sales were satisfactory, it said.
